01.reason: The sages gather in Lod, a question is put, they disagree and then reach a joint conclusion. It is almost all speech, with some conflict and a resolution, so borderline.

02.reason: Relatives come before R. Yohanan, who advises them, and he later regrets helping them. That is mostly a ruling, but his change of mind adds some change, so borderline rather than not.

03.reason: Statements by Rav and R. Hiyya about their own eiruv practice. Speech cited as a legal source, with no event.

04.reason: A setting (Ravina finds Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak leaning on a door) that only frames a legal dilemma. Under the Shabbat 147a ruling a setting plus a question is not a story.

05.reason: A case comes before the Sages and they rule. Coming before them is the only event, which is R-C0's limit.

06.reason: Cases came before Rabbi and R. Yishmael and they ruled, followed by scholarly discussion of the rulings. There is no event beyond bringing the case and no real conflict.

07.reason: A man's incidental remark about his and his mother's captivity leads Rabbi to permit her to marry into the priesthood. It is essentially a case and a ruling, but the narrated captivity and the change in her status keep it borderline.

08.reason: An incident alluded to inside the legal discussion: a man held a feast on the ninetieth day and Rava made him forfeit it. The ruling is an act with a consequence, but the incident is only sketched.

09.reason: A man testifies before R. Ami, they exchange questions and answers, and R. Ami rules. Coming before the rabbi and his ruling is all that happens.

10.reason: Rav Yosef says he has not heard a teaching and Abaye reminds him that he taught it. Ordinary scholarly dialogue with no event.

11.reason: One line of background (Rami bar Hama's sister was married to Rav Avya) with no event in the passage itself.

12.reason: A report of what Rav Kahana did with an orphan's beer, given as his practice and reasoning. Nothing follows from it.

13.reason: An incident cited as evidence: the tumtum of Biri was operated on and later fathered seven children. It has events and change but is only alluded to inside a legal argument.

14.reason: Minyamin's statement of his own status and his marriage plans, cited as a legal source. It is speech and intention, not a narrated event.

15.reason: The students ask R. Eliezer a question and he answers. The register rules this exact passage (Yevamot 78b:9) not a story.

16.reason: An incident only alluded to: a debtor hid his money behind a gentile, so the Sages forced him to sell his land. It has an action and a consequence but is recounted only briefly inside legal discussion.

17.reason: Two linked incidents before Reish Lakish and R. Yohanan. Reish Lakish realizes R. Elazar had withheld the source, looks at him harshly and rebukes him: conflict, an emotional reaction and a change.

18.reason: Rav Yosef says he has not heard a teaching and Abaye recites what he had taught them. Scholarly dialogue with no narrated event.

19.reason: One act (residents put a rolled mat in an alleyway in Sura) followed only by Rav Hisda's legal critique. Nothing else happens.

20.reason: A dialogue between R. Yohanan and R. Elazar with disagreement, R. Yohanan's grief, and R. Elazar finding him a remedy. It is mainly speech but has conflict and an emotional change, like Ketubot 112a:11.
